body.statement: Can one choose deterministic schedules \(p_n,L_n,q_n\), polynomially bounded in \(n\) and \(\lceil\log_2(1/\alpha)\rceil\), with \(T_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\ge B+\sigma\sqrt{12\log(e+n)}+1\), and compose \(\mathsf{Enc}_{p_n,L_n}\) with the deterministic dyadic certificate so that the resulting measurable interval \(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}}\), evaluated on the original real Gaussian blocks, satisfies \(\liminf_n\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}P\{\theta_n\in I_n^{\mathrm{fp}}\}\ge1-\alpha\), \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}P(\kappa_n=1)=o(n^{-1})\), \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_n]/w_n\to0\), and \(\limsup_n\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}})]/w_n\le K_\alpha\)? Along every sequence \(P_n\in\mathcal P_n\) with \(b_n/a_n\to0\), must \(\varepsilon_n/a_n\to0\) and \(\operatorname{length}(I_n^{\mathrm{fp}})/[2\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)a_n]\to1\) in \(P_n\)-probability? On \(\kappa_n=0\), the certificate must propagate the coordinate error \(2^{-p_n-1}\) into \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\) and satisfy \(I_n^{\mathrm{out}}(X,R,C)\subseteq I_n^{\mathrm{fp}}\) and \(0\le\varepsilon_n\le2\Delta_n^{\mathrm{num}}\); on \(\kappa_n=1\), it must return \([-M_0,M_0]\). Along every sequence \(P_n\in\mathcal P_n\) with \(r=1\) and \(u=v=0\), the \(P_n\)-expectation of each recorded summand of \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{enc}}\) and \(\Delta_n^{\mathrm{arith}}\), the fallback contribution \(M_0\mathbf 1\{\kappa_n=1\}\), and \(\varepsilon_n\) must be \(o(n^{-1})\).
body.justification: This is the genuinely open statistical last-mile theorem: it must transfer a deterministic dyadic certificate to continuously distributed observations without changing the Gaussian model.
body.gap: Panel papers assume exact operations, while verified numerics begins from finite encodings; no source supplies a measurable clipping-and-rounding interface whose propagated error is negligible in probability and expectation at the panel transition scale.
body.consumer: A positive answer yields software whose reported CAST-style counterfactual intervals inherit coverage under the stated continuous Gaussian experiment rather than under an artificial dyadic-data model.
